owner.headline: Repeated password guessing on {agent_name}.
owner.what_we_know: {count}+ wrong passwords in {window_minutes} minutes from one address. Not a confirmed break-in yet.
owner.why: One correct guess opens patient records. Blocking that address stops the guessing.

steps.text: Review the block request, or call your IT contact (saved in ShieldMate).

fallback_reword.headline: Someone keeps trying to get into {agent_name} by guessing its password.
fallback_reword.why: If they guess right, they can open patient records.

owner.headline: Files on {agent_name} are being locked. This looks like ransomware.
owner.what_we_know: {files_renamed} files were renamed to .locked in {window_minutes} minute. Treat it as real until IT says otherwise.
owner.why: Locked files can stop appointments, billing and patient records.

steps.text: Unplug {agent_name} from the network. Leave it switched on.
Call your IT contact (saved in ShieldMate).
Test your backup before you restore anything.

fallback_reword.headline: Files on {agent_name} are being locked, which looks like ransomware.
fallback_reword.why: Locked files can stop appointments, billing and patient records.

owner.headline: A phishing email was flagged on {agent_name}.
owner.what_we_know: {count} suspicious email(s) in {window_minutes} minute(s). Treat it as phishing until IT says otherwise.
owner.why: One clicked link can open the doctor's own account - the most important one in the clinic.

steps.text: Do not delete the email or clear the log - keep it for IT.
Call your IT contact (saved in ShieldMate).

front_desk.headline: A phishing email was flagged on {agent_name}.
front_desk.why: One clicked link can let someone into this computer and the clinic's accounts.

steps.text: Do not open the flagged email or its links.
Leave the email in place for IT.

billing.headline: A phishing email was flagged on {agent_name}.
billing.why: One clicked link can let someone into this computer and the clinic's accounts.

steps.text: Do not open the flagged email or its links.
Leave the email in place for IT.

fallback_reword.headline: A phishing email was flagged on {agent_name}.
fallback_reword.why: One clicked link can open the doctor's own account.

owner.headline: Someone else has signed in to your email.
owner.what_we_know: Your email was just opened from a place the clinic has never used. The password was probably typed into a fake page.
owner.why: Whoever has it can read your email and send messages to patients in the clinic's name.

steps.text: Change your email password now, from your phone or a different computer, not {agent_name}.
Call your IT contact (saved in ShieldMate) to check the account.
Don't use {agent_name} until IT says it's safe.

fallback_reword.headline: Someone else has got into your email.
fallback_reword.why: They can send messages to patients pretending to be the clinic.

owner.headline: Your email is sending messages to patients.
owner.what_we_know: {count} emails went out from your account in {window_minutes} minutes, asking patients to pay a fee.
owner.why: Patients may pay a scammer believing it's the clinic, and their details have been seen.

steps.text: Change your email password now, from your phone or a different computer.
Call your IT contact (saved in ShieldMate) to stop the emails.
Start the patient-data breach record: patient details were seen.

front_desk.headline: Patients may call about a fake payment message from the clinic.
front_desk.what_we_know: Dr. Rao's email has been sending messages asking patients to pay a fee. The messages are fake.
front_desk.why: Patients trust the clinic. A clear answer stops them losing money.

steps.text: Tell every caller the message is fake and not to pay. Write down who called.
Tap Done: Dr. Rao is told.

billing.headline: Patients may have paid a fake fee in the clinic's name.
billing.what_we_know: Dr. Rao's email has been sending messages asking patients to pay a fee. The messages are fake.
billing.why: The sooner a patient reports it, the better the chance of getting the money back.

steps.text: If a patient says they paid, tell them to call 1930 now.
Write down every patient who says they paid.

fallback_reword.headline: Your email is sending fake payment requests to patients.
fallback_reword.why: Patients may pay a scammer thinking it's the clinic.

front_desk.headline: A program that lets someone control this computer was installed on {agent_name}.
front_desk.what_we_know: It appeared a moment ago. If someone phoned and asked you to install it, that call was a scam.
front_desk.why: Whoever is on the other end can see and click everything on this computer, including billing and patient records.

steps.text: Pull the network cable out of the back of {agent_name} (or turn its Wi-Fi off). Leave it switched on.
If a caller asked you to install it, hang up. Only call back on numbers saved in ShieldMate.
Tap Done: Dr. Rao is told.

owner.headline: A remote-control program was installed on {agent_name}.
owner.what_we_know: Staff may have been tricked by a fake "tech support" phone call.
owner.why: Someone outside could control the computer used for check-in and billing.

steps.text: Make sure {agent_name} is unplugged from the network. Leave it switched on.
Call your IT contact (saved in ShieldMate) to remove the program.

fallback_reword.headline: Someone may be able to control {agent_name} from outside.
fallback_reword.why: They could see billing and patient records.

front_desk.headline: Someone outside is controlling {agent_name} right now.
front_desk.what_we_know: The mouse may be moving by itself. This is the program from the fake support call.
front_desk.why: Every second it stays connected, they can open more.

steps.text: Pull the network cable out now. Leave the computer switched on.
Call your IT contact (saved in ShieldMate).

owner.headline: Someone outside is controlling {agent_name} right now.
owner.what_we_know: A remote-control program installed after a fake support call is in use.
owner.why: They can open whatever that computer can open.

steps.text: Make sure {agent_name} is unplugged from the network. Leave it switched on.
Call your IT contact (saved in ShieldMate) to remove the program.
Change passwords that were typed on {agent_name}, from a different device.
Ask the bank to hold payments until IT says it's safe, in case a banking password was typed on {agent_name}.

fallback_reword.headline: Someone outside is using {agent_name} right now.
fallback_reword.why: They can open whatever that computer can open.

owner.headline: Files are being copied out of {agent_name}.
owner.what_we_know: {count} files were sent to an outside address in {window_minutes} minutes.
owner.why: Patient files that leave the clinic count as a personal-data breach.

steps.text: Make sure {agent_name} is unplugged from the network. Leave it switched on.
Call your IT contact (saved in ShieldMate).
Report to CERT-In within 6 hours.
Start the patient-data breach record.

front_desk.headline: Files are being copied out of {agent_name}.
front_desk.what_we_know: The program from the fake support call is sending files outside the clinic.
front_desk.why: Patient files may be leaving the clinic right now.

steps.text: Pull the network cable out now. Leave the computer switched on.
Write down the caller's number and what he asked for.

fallback_reword.headline: Files are leaving {agent_name} for somewhere outside the clinic.
fallback_reword.why: Patient files leaving the clinic is a data breach.

billing.headline: An email asks the clinic to pay a supplier's new bank account.
billing.what_we_know: This is how supplier payment scams start. Look closely at the sender's address below: one letter or dash different is a common trick.
billing.why: Money sent to a scammer's account is very hard to get back.

steps.text: Don't pay. Call the supplier on the number you already have, not one in the email.
Tell Dr. Rao before any payment to new bank details.

owner.headline: A supplier email asks to change their bank details.
owner.what_we_know: Change-of-bank emails are the most common way clinics lose money to scammers.
owner.why: Money sent to a scammer's account is very hard to get back.

steps.text: Make sure nobody pays new bank details until the supplier is called on their old number.

fallback_reword.headline: A supplier email asks the clinic to pay a new bank account.
fallback_reword.why: It may be a scam; check by phone before paying.

billing.headline: A payment to the new bank account has been sent.
billing.what_we_know: The money went to the account in the supplier email. If it was a scam, the next hour matters most.
billing.why: The bank can often freeze money soon after it is paid, before it is moved on.

steps.text: Call the bank's fraud line now and ask them to stop the payment.
Call 1930, the cyber-fraud helpline, or report at cybercrime.gov.in.
Keep the emails and the payment receipt.

owner.headline: A payment went to a possible scammer's bank account.
owner.what_we_know: A payment went to the new bank details from the supplier email.
owner.why: The bank can often freeze money soon after it is paid.

steps.text: Call the bank's fraud line with Ravi now.
Make sure it is reported on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in.

fallback_reword.headline: Money may have gone to a scammer's bank account.
fallback_reword.why: Calling the bank quickly can freeze it.
